Subject: Post-demo: validate monthly allocation window & PO gating for LumenHealth pilot

Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size pricing and the procurement path: 

Key call notes:
- Use case: clinical summarization + search for provider/ops workflows (latency-sensitive).
- Expected query shape: short prompts, avg. response length ~150 tokens, bursty during business hours.
- Ops requirements: SOC 2 + audit logs requested by procurement team.

As discussed, we need two pieces to finalize a recommended monthly pricing band and procurement lane: 
1) Monthly token volume estimate (min / expected / max). Rough numbers are fine — e.g., 50M / 200M / 500M.
2) Procurement gating: PO thresholds, invoice terms (Net30/Net45), and any internal approval gates (legal review threshold, e.g., >$100k/month).

Prelim economics and what to expect from us (attached): Redwood-Pilot-Pricing-Overview.pdf includes pay-as-you-go versus committed tiers and an example computation for 1M-token unit pricing. If you can confirm the two items above, I’ll run our model and send a short banded estimate with recommended commit options.

Next steps I propose:
- You share the monthly estimate + procurement constraints by Tue (20 Jul).
- I’ll return a 1‑page spend-band estimate + recommended procurement path by Wed (21 Jul).
- If numbers align, schedule a procurement intro with your PO team (we can join).

Thanks — appreciate the time.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Vanessa —

Appreciate the clear recap. From our side, initial roughs below (we'll validate with analytics):
- Monthly tokens (approx): min 100M / expected 250M / max 400M.
- Procurement: standard policy — PO required for contracts >= $30k/month; legal review kicks in for > $150k/month. Standard payment terms Net30. SOC 2 + evidence required for security/compliance signoff.

Regarding unit economics, our internal target is around $1,200 per 1M tokens (we arrived at that from product-margin goals). Is that within reach with a short pilot/commit or would it require a Dedicated arrangement? Also, what are the lead times for getting SOC 2 artifacts and audit logs? Procurement will need those up front.

We did not receive the pricing PDF as an editable spreadsheet — if you could provide a banded estimate for the volumes above (and an XLSX with the calc), that will help our finance team move quickly.

Alex — thanks for the numbers and the procurement constraints. Helpful. Attaching a short XLSX that walks the math. Highlights below so procurement has clarity immediately: 

Pricing summary (illustrative) — base pay-as-you-go (no commit): $1,800 per 1M tokens.
- 3-month committed volume (tiered): 10% discount -> $1,620 per 1M tokens.
- 6-month committed volume (tiered): 20% discount -> $1,440 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated/reserved capacity: custom pricing; at 300M+ tokens/month we can evaluate a Dedicated pool to approach $1,200 per 1M depending on burst profile and SLA needs.

Estimated monthly spend (based on your 100M / 250M / 400M):
- 100M -> PAYG: ~$180,000/mo | 6-mo commit (20%): ~$144,000/mo
- 250M -> PAYG: ~$450,000/mo | 6-mo commit (20%): ~$360,000/mo
- 400M -> PAYG: ~$720,000/mo | 6-mo commit (20%): ~$576,000/mo

Procurement lane (pilot vs. production):
- Pilot (3 months, invoice or CC): we can run pilot without PO; monthly invoicing or CC accepted.
- Production (recommended for >$30k/mo): PO + Net30.
- Legal review threshold: contracts above $150k/month will generally require a legal checklist; we can fast-track for proofs of compliance (SOC 2, audit logs).

Next steps I recommend: 
1) I've attached LumenHealth-Monthly-Band-Estimate.xlsx with the cells editable — please share with finance.
2) If your target is $1,200 /1M, let's schedule a quick pricing calibration call Thu (22 Jul) to discuss committing structure vs Dedicated sizing.
3) Marissa (cc) will prepare a procurement packet and SOC2 evidence bundle we can share with your procurement team.

Links: HubSpot record and a preliminary DocuSign envelope (SOW skeleton) are below.

Thanks — I’ll also include the short one-page summary as a Drive link if you prefer.

—
